summary: Classic pivot points with support and resistance levels from the prior period: Traditional, Fibonacci, Camarilla or Woodie.
overview: Pivot Points draw a central pivot (P) with resistance (R) levels above and support (S) levels below, for each period on the price chart.
The pivot is orange, resistances red and supports green.
how: Traditional: P = (high + low + close) / 3 of the prior period. R1 = 2P - low, S1 = 2P - high, R2 = P + (high - low), S2 = P - (high - low), and so on. Fibonacci adds 38.2%, 61.8% and 100% of the prior range to P. Camarilla scales the range around the prior close. Woodie weights the close more.
Auto timeframe uses daily pivots up to 15-minute bars, weekly on other intraday bars, monthly on daily bars, and yearly above.
use: Some traders watch P as the line between bullish and bearish bias for the period.
Use R and S levels as areas where price may react.
Compare types to see which levels match the symbol's swings.
Use weekly or monthly pivots for a wider view.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
Levels are fixed for the period once it starts.
